The Crow Indians are presently served by facilities and personnel of the Indian Health Service. An increased Crow population, as well as an anticipated higher level of awareness of health care benefits, will require a substantial expansion of these services.
There will also be a need to expand hospital services. Using a standard of 4 beds per 1,000 population, the increased population would require about 20 more beds by 1990 and about 32 more beds by 2000.

Public Assistance - Dependency on public assistance among the Crow Indians may decline due to increased employment income. In addition, if continued substantial per capita royalty payments are made to the individual Crow Indians this could result in stable income which could significantly reduce existing dependency on welfare. The manner in which these payments are made will have a significant bearing on any reduction in dependency on public assistance.
Although an initial decline is anticipated, during the construction phase, as the mine enters the operations phase the amount of assistance required through welfare and unemployment compensation is very likely to increase if the continuing operational activities do not absorb the resident construction labor force.
